newsitem.title: MEXICO: CARSO GLOBAL TELECOM SHARES UP SHARPLY.
newsitem.headline: CARSO GLOBAL TELECOM SHARES UP SHARPLY.

text.p: Shares listed by holding company Carso Global Telecom (CGT) rose sharply in mid-morning trade on the Mexican bourse on Thursday.
CGT shares gained 1.70 pesos to 34.70, and were fending off a bout of profit-taking on the broad market.

Dealers said the stock was in demand following press reports that Carlos Slim, owner of a related company, Grupo Carso, had bought a three percent stake in Apple Computer Inc before the share price was driven up on Wednesday by news of an investment from Microsoft Corp.

"If the investment was made, then the most likely vehicle was Orient Star, a subsidiary of Carso Global Telecom. It's right up their alley as a high-tech stock," said an analyst, who declined to be named.

The analyst estimated CGT would have made some $50 million from the acquisition of Apple stock. Nonetheless, he added, this would only partly offset a quarter-on-quarter decline of $150 million in Orient Star's portfolio position as of the second quarter of 1997.
"If true, it's good but not wonderful news," he said.
A spokesman for Slim was not immediately available for comment.
